title: Global extreme poverty is declining only marginally while progress remains sharply uneven across regions and exposed to measurement revision
source_unit: World Bank September 2026 Global Poverty Update using the Poverty and Inequality Platform
geography: Global and regional poverty estimates through 2024 with nowcasts for 2025 and 2026

denominator.unit: world population under the World Bank international poverty-line framework

people_in_extreme_poverty.unit: people living below $3.00 per person per day in 2021 PPP

global_rate.unit: share of world population below the international extreme-poverty line

coverage.value: survey coverage sufficient across all regions in 2022–2024

observations.method: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform global and regional estimates combining household-survey data with auxiliary national-accounts, population, and price data.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate depends on poverty-line choice, purchasing-power-parity conversion, survey coverage, imputation, price data, and model harmonization; it is not a direct count of every person’s current resources.
observations.subgroup: People and households below the international extreme-poverty line, with regional differences and data-coverage constraints retained.
observations.counterinterpretation: A global rate can decline while poverty remains severe or rises in particular regions; income poverty also does not capture multidimensional deprivation, insecurity, services, or agency.

denominator.unit: global extreme-poverty estimate and World Bank nowcast frame

observations.method: World Bank nowcasts for 2025 and 2026 based on national-accounts projections from the June 2026 Global Economic Prospects and the latest available poverty estimates.
observations.uncertainty: The 2025 and 2026 figures are nowcasts rather than completed survey estimates and are sensitive to growth, inflation, distribution, conflict, and future data revisions.
observations.subgroup: Global population, with outcomes likely to differ by region, income group, labor market, prices, conflict exposure, and public-service access.
observations.counterinterpretation: A small projected decline need not mean meaningful improvement in lived security, consumption smoothing, nutrition, or access to services for households near the poverty line.

denominator.unit: global and regional poverty comparison frame

high_poverty_regions.value: Sub-Saharan Africa and the Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the regions with the highest or rising extreme-poverty pressure in the release

revision.value: 10.4% to 10.1%, or about 846.8 million to 824.3 million people, compared with the March 2026 vintage

revision_drivers.value: new household surveys, revised country-year estimates, and updated national accounts, population projections, and consumer price indices

observations.method: Descriptive comparison of the September 2026 Poverty and Inequality Platform vintage with the March 2026 vintage and regional trend framing.
observations.uncertainty: Revisions improve or alter estimates without necessarily indicating real-time changes in household welfare; regional comparisons remain dependent on comparable data and modeled coverage.
observations.subgroup: Regions with high poverty, conflict and displacement exposure, limited survey coverage, or substantial revisions to the underlying data.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved measurement can lower an estimate without reducing deprivation, while a rising regional rate can reflect new data and boundary changes as well as real worsening.

related_sources.claim: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform provides the underlying poverty estimates and data interface.
World Bank Global Economic Prospects provides the macroeconomic projections used for the 2025 and 2026 nowcasts.

boundary: This record adds a material-pressure and inequality signal linking extreme-poverty measurement, household resources, regional divergence, conflict and data coverage, nowcasting, and revision. It is a World Bank modeled estimate and nowcast, not respondent-level ingestion, a current household panel, multidimensional deprivation measure, causal poverty intervention evaluation, or proof of lived welfare change.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official World Bank Data Blog update was reviewed for the poverty line, 2024 estimate, 2025–2026 nowcasts, regional divergence, survey coverage, vintage revision, and revision drivers; modeled estimates and projections were kept distinct from direct observations.
